title: Yara and the Oath
premise: Jude Yarrow has spent a lifetime stealing memories to survive, trading other people's pasts for passage along the smuggler roads of Thornfell. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, the kingdom of Cael is erased from every map and memory but Jude's own—because the memories they stole include the king's dying confession. Hunted by the Wardens who unmade the country and shadowed by Sera, a knight who remembers nothing yet trusts Jude anyway, Jude must reach the Door of Returning before the last stolen memory burns out. In the end, Jude must choose between restoring the kingdom and keeping the only proof that they ever mattered, and they pay the price of survival by giving up their own name so that truth—and justice outside the law—can outlive them.
about_author: Sable Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who grew up in mining towns where borders were drawn and redrawn over living people. They write fantasy about outsiders who carry what nations would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Jude. On a rain-slicked smuggler road, Jude trades a stolen memory of first love for safe passage through Thornfell, establishing their gift and their rules: never keep, never feel. The beat is wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The stars go out mid-crossing; the border wards shatter like glass behind them. A refugee column stumbles past, unable to say where they came from. Jude realizes their own memories of Cael are intact—the only ones. Beat: dread dawning into resolve.

chapters.title: What the King Confessed
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Hiding in a waystation, Jude examines the oldest stolen memory they carry: the king's deathbed confession about the Door of Returning and the bargain that erased his realm. Beat: horror at holding something worth killing for.

chapters.title: The Warden's Hounds
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Grey-cloaked Wardens sweep the pass, pulling memories from travelers to find 'the carrier.' Jude escapes by feeding a hound a decoy memory, but is marked. Beat: hunted, resourceful, first blood drawn.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Sera. A knight wakes on a battlefield with no name and one instinct: protect the person in the thief's coat she keeps dreaming of. She tracks Jude through the fog-choked lowlands. Beat: disorientation sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Sera corners Jude; neither can explain why they trust each other. Jude offers her fragments of Cael from stolen memories in exchange for her sword. Beat: reluctant alliance, tenderness neither will name.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The map roads to the capital now lead nowhere; Jude navigates by remembered smuggler routes instead. They shelter with an old fence, Maren, who half-remembers Jude as a child. Beat: grief for a homeland only two people mourn.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Wardens raid Maren's cellar. Sera fights without knowing why her body remembers war; Maren dies buying them time, whispering Jude's real childhood name. Beat: first true loss, guilt igniting Jude's self-loathing.

chapters.title: The Memory Market
chapters.summary: POV Jude. In the free city of Vask, memories are currency. Jude barters for a guide to the Door and glimpses their own childhood memory for sale—a thing they never sold. Someone is selling pieces of them. Beat: violation and paranoia.

chapters.title: The Broker of Lost Things
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sara confronts the broker Ossian, who reveals he bought Jude's memories from a Warden defector—and that Sera was the king's executioner before the erasure. Beat: betrayal cracking the alliance's foundation.

chapters.title: What You Did Before
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude learns Sera carried out the king's death, believing it mercy during a plague the Wardens engineered. Fury, then terrible understanding: both were tools. Beat: rage transmuting into shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: POV Jude. They meet Ilse, the Warden defector, in Vask's undercity. She explains the erasure ritual: a country unmade needs an anchor of memory, and Jude is it. The Door opens only for the anchor. Beat: revelation reframing everything—Jude isn't hiding from fate, they are the fate.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Wardens storm Vask. Ilse is captured covering their escape; Sera holds the gate alone and finally remembers her own name in the fighting. Beat: sacrifice, and identity reclaimed through action rather than memory.

chapters.title: Into the White Mountains
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Fleeing into snowbound highlands, Jude begins losing their own memories—the erasure consuming the anchor. They teach Sera the route in case they forget. Beat: ticking clock made flesh; intimacy deepening through urgency.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Sera. They find a village of erased survivors who persist by telling their stories aloud nightly. An elder recognizes the king's confession in Jude and begs them not to open the Door—some erasures are mercies. Beat: moral complication; doubt planted.

chapters.title: Ilse's Truth
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Rescued Ilse confesses the full design: the Wardens didn't destroy Cael—they quarantined a god the king had bound, and opening the Door frees it. Restoring the kingdom may doom everyone inside it. Beat: the central choice crystallized: truth versus loyalty to the dead.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sera, remembering her oath to the king, chooses justice over obedience: the king asked to be killed because he could not bear to release the god, and the Wardens' answer—erasing everyone—was worse. She breaks her sword-oath formally. Beat: theme resolved in miniature; loyalty redefined as truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Last Road
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Final ascent to the Door of Returning, pursued by the High Warden. Jude has forgotten Maren, forgotten Vask, is forgetting their own face. Sera carries their memories aloud like a litany. Beat: elegiac determination; love as archive.

chapters.title: The Door of Returning
chapters.summary: POV Jude. At the Door, the High Warden offers Jude a trade: walk away and keep surviving, anonymous forever. Jude refuses—survival without truth is just a longer erasure. Battle at the threshold. Beat: climax begins; the theme stated in flesh.

chapters.title: The Name I Give Away
chapters.summary: POV Jude. To open the Door safely, the anchor must be spent. Jude pours their stolen hoard—and their own name and past—into the lock. Cael returns to maps and minds; the god stays bound because the king's confession, now public, lets the living renegotiate the binding. Beat: climax and sacrifice fused.

chapters.title: After the Stars Return
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Cael exists again; its people remember. Sera finds Jude alive but nameless, a stranger even to themselves, and begins telling them their story—the village's nightly rite, continued. Beat: bittersweet resolution; justice served outside any law.

chapters.title: Yarrow, Planted Again
chapters.summary: POV Jude (mostly). Relearning themselves through Sera's telling, Jude chooses a new name—Yarrow, after the healing weed—and steals one last memory freely given: Sera's memory of them, kept on purpose this time. Beat: quiet hope; the price paid becomes a seed.
